title: G-Drive wins Monza as DragonSpeed takes a 1-2
dek: Ryo Hirakawa, Memo Rojas and Leo Roussel won the 4 Hours of Monza in G-Drive's Oreca #22, 2.245 seconds clear of DragonSpeed's #21 after a late drive-through penalty.

chapters.title: Monza returns, with Le Mans a month away
text: The European Le Mans Series arrived at Monza on 14 May 2017 for round two of the season, its first race at the Italian circuit since 2008 and, for 17 of the crews, a last proper rehearsal before the Le Mans 24 Hours a month later. Thirty-six cars were entered, including twelve LMP2s in the first year of the new-generation prototype rules: five Ligier JS P217s, four Oreca 07s and three Dallara P217s, all running Gibson engines.

Silverstone had set the terms. United's Ligier #32 won after Filipe Albuquerque tracked down and passed Ryo Hirakawa's G-Drive Oreca late on, the G-Drive car having lost tyre performance in the closing stint. High Class Racing's Dallara took third on its European debut, while DragonSpeed's #21 Oreca, on pole at Silverstone, slid to tenth with mechanical problems. Both DragonSpeed-run cars arrived with something to prove, and Cetilar Villorba Corse, whose Dallara had been the fastest of its type in qualifying, was racing at home.

The entry shuffled slightly. Olivier Pla made his first start of the season for IDEC Sport in the #28 Ligier after missing Silverstone for his WEC commitments, while Panis Barthez Competition ran the #23 Ligier as a two-driver crew because Matthieu Vaxiviere was injured in training. Tockwith Motorsports returned to a two-man line-up in the #34 Ligier, with Phil Hanson and Nigel Moore, after the team's WEC outing at Spa. The weather was gloomy with storms forecast, and heavy rain briefly hit Friday's first practice, which Hirakawa topped for G-Drive. Nicolas Lapierre led the second session in the sister DragonSpeed car on 1:37.258, with the Graff #39 second and Albuquerque third.

chapters.title: Graff's surprise pole
text: Enzo Guibbert put the Graff Oreca #39 on pole with a 1:36.526 late in the session, the Silver-rated driver admitting afterwards that the result felt incredible. It was Graff's first LMP2 pole in only its second race in the class. Lapierre had looked a likely pole-sitter after a 1:36.641 on his first flying lap, but ended up 0.115 seconds short on the front row of the grid.

Hirakawa was third for G-Drive after his final lap was spoiled when he came up behind a slower High Class Dallara. Albuquerque was fourth in the best of the Ligiers, 0.346 off the pace, and Andrea Pizzitola took fifth for Algarve Pro Racing, also in a Ligier. Andrea Belicchi was the fastest Dallara in sixth for Cetilar Villorba Corse, with Richard Bradley seventh in the second Graff, which meant the top seven were covered by less than a second. Tockwith, High Class, IDEC, Panis Barthez and Racing Team Nederland completed the grid in that order from eighth to twelfth. The wider paddock had its own poles: Wayne Boyd led LMP3 for United and Matt Griffin the GTE class for Spirit of Race.

chapters.title: Graff leads, G-Drive stumbles
text: The race started at 13:30. Guibbert held the lead from pole, with Lapierre in close attendance, but G-Drive made a poor start: Memo Rojas dropped from third to fifth in the first ten minutes. After eight laps the first Full Course Yellow was needed when the LMP3 Ligiers of Panis Barthez (#16) and AT Racing (#9) tangled at Turn 8, and Lapierre lost time by going onto the grass to avoid them.

Bradley, meanwhile, was tearing up the order from seventh on the grid. He set the fastest lap of the race on lap 5 and was challenging for the lead when a drive-through penalty for a jump start knocked him back, and an electrical fault then stopped the Graff #40 on track. It restarted but was in trouble for the rest of the afternoon. In the opening hour Lapierre also undercut the pole-sitting Graff to take over the lead, while Cetilar Villorba Corse and High Class fought over third.

chapters.title: Three yellows and a G-Drive pit stop
text: The race was interrupted twice more, both times by LMP3 incidents. A collision between the United Ligier #2 and the AT Racing car brought the second Full Course Yellow with roughly two hours 50 minutes to go, and about five minutes after the restart the Oregon Team Norma #10 hit the barrier at Turn 1 for the third.

The yellows reshuffled LMP2. Graff pitted just before the green flag and Guibbert fell to fifth, while G-Drive, which had stopped under the first two neutralisations, switched Rojas for Leo Roussel at the second stop. The Frenchman hurried through the field, passing the Cetilar Dallara and then, with the help of traffic, the DragonSpeed Oreca to take the lead. At the half-way mark the G-Drive car led, with Cetilar second.

chapters.title: Electrical gremlins and a DragonSpeed lull
text: The new generation of LMP2 cars was suffering from electrical problems. Cetilar Villorba Corse, a clear contender for the win, stopped on track with Belicchi at the wheel with around 90 minutes left, rejoining but losing its chance of victory. Tockwith's Ligier made repeated visits to the garage, the Algarve Ligier also hit trouble, and the Graff #40 had already suffered several resets.

DragonSpeed's #21 car had a quieter spell. Henrik Hedman's middle stint dropped it outside the top five, and Matt McMurry, in the Algarve Ligier, passed Hedman for third just before the handover to Ben Hanley. G-Drive meanwhile extended its advantage, and by the final stint the lead was a comfortable cushion of at least 45 seconds.

chapters.title: The penalty that did not matter
text: With Hirakawa in the car for the final stint it looked a cruise, until G-Drive was handed a drive-through penalty for failing to respect the speed limit under a Full Course Yellow. Hirakawa came back out still in front, but the gap had melted to roughly 20 seconds. Behind him Hanley was among the quickest men on the track in the final hour.

chapters.title: Hanley pounces, Hirakawa holds on
text: The High Class Dallara of Anders Fjordbach inherited second place, but a late splash of fuel with around ten minutes left dropped it into the clutches of the DragonSpeed Oreca. Hanley passed it in the closing laps, up the inside through traffic at the second chicane, and set off after the leader. Hirakawa slowed over the last laps, and the gap at the flag was 2.245 seconds, G-Drive's first win of the season and a 1-2 for the DragonSpeed operation.

Fjordbach and Dennis Andersen took third, 7.215 seconds off the winner and their second podium in as many races. Graff's #39 was fourth, 33.980 seconds back after leading in the early running, and Cetilar Villorba Corse's Dallara came home fifth despite its stoppage. Albuquerque brought the United Ligier home sixth after a difficult day, ahead of Panis Barthez in seventh. Bradley's Graff was eighth, one lap down, and Algarve Pro Racing stopped on the final lap, which left the car not classified despite 131 laps run.

chapters.title: A historic result for G-Drive and DragonSpeed
text: It was a landmark afternoon for the American DragonSpeed operation, which took the first 1-2 overall in the European Le Mans Series since the competition evolved from the Le Mans Series in 2012, and the first in Le Mans Series history since Peugeot at Imola in 2011. It was also the first European Le Mans Series win for the Oreca 07, and the first ELMS victory for Rojas. G-Drive became the fifth team to win in either the ELMS or the WEC under the G-Drive banner after Delta-ADR, Oak Racing, Jota Sport and TDS Racing.

The win turned the LMP2 championship around. With second at Silverstone and victory at Monza, the #22 crew of Rojas, Roussel and Hirakawa led the standings on 43 points, ten ahead of the United Ligier #32 of Albuquerque, de Sadeleer and Owen on 33 after the team's sixth place. High Class Racing's Dallara, with two thirds, was third on 30 points, and the DragonSpeed #21 car was fourth on 20. Nearly 20,000 spectators attended the weekend.

There was an immediate sense of what lay ahead. Jose Gutierrez was confirmed in the #22 G-Drive Oreca for Le Mans in the seat Roussel occupied at Monza, while the #21 car added Felix Rosenqvist to Hedman and Hanley. Graff kept its ELMS line-ups for both cars, with James Winslow added to the #39. Bradley told ELMS television of his concern over the electrical problems of the new LMP2s, which struck at least four cars during the race.
The European Le Mans Series now broke for Le Mans on 17-18 June, and the next round is the 4 Hours of the Red Bull Ring in Austria on 23 July.

facts.v: Enzo Guibbert took pole with 1:36.526, 0.115s ahead of Lapierre, in only Graff's second race in LMP2.
